messages:
maria: FYI I pushed the new 'runtime + infra' dashboard to the org Grafana. Need input on alert thresholds and which panels should page vs slack. Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/runtime-infra-new

jake: saw it, love the layout. main questions: which of these are SLO-driven (page) vs ops-only (slack). p99 latency, error-rate, and SLO burn rate are the obvious ones.

oliver: agree. my baseline proposal:
- page for SLO burn_rate > 3 for 15m
- page for error_rate > 1% for 5m (service-level)
- slack for p99 spikes unless sustained > 800ms for 10m

priya: +1 but let's be explicit about burn math. our SLO is 99.9% over 30d. That corresponds to an error budget of ~0.1%. If burn_rate > 3 that means we're burning 3x the budget which is pretty urgent. Suggest page for burn_rate >= 4 for 1h or >= 6 for 15m.

maria: good point. we want to avoid too many pages during short bursts. can we use a composite monitor: page only if burn_rate AND error_rate both high OR burn sustained?

jake: yep Datadog supports composite monitors. Example query idea (PromQL-like):
```
# burn rate estimate (pseudo)
burn_rate = increase(errors_total[1h]) / (error_budget * 1h)
# p99 query
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

oliver: for implem I'll convert to datadog monitor syntax. also need to map to pager policy. propose this YAML snippet for the oncall router: 
```yaml
- name: inference-runtime-slo-burn
  match: service:inference AND monitor:burn_rate
  severity: page
  conditions:
    - metric: burn_rate
      op: ">="
      value: 4
      window: 1h
- name: inference-errors
  match: service:inference AND metric:error_rate
  severity: page
  conditions:
    - metric: error_rate
      op: ">="
      value: 1
      window: 5m
- name: p99-latency
  match: service:inference AND metric:p99_latency
  severity: slack
  conditions:
    - metric: p99_latency
      op: ">="
      value: 800ms
      window: 10m
```

priya: runbook owners also need to be attached. I volunteer to own the SLO burn runbook. can we add a tag/label so runbook link appears in pages?

maria: yes add `runbook: /runbooks/inference-slo` to the policy. also we should attach escalation steps and customer-impact notes.

sre-bot: Incident template available: /templates/slo-burn. Use `incident:create --template slo-burn --severity P1` to create.

jake: implementation plan: I'll create the monitors in datadog this week. Oliver can review and QA. Priya will draft runbook updates. Tom can validate pager routing config in staging.

tom: I can validate routing. note: org pager has a rate-limit of 3 pages per 10m to primary. if we page too eagerly we will get throttled. suggest grouping similar monitors into a single alert to reduce churn.

liz: +1 on grouping. also add a non-paging 'health' dashboard alert to slack for kv-cache hitrate < 85% for 15m — ops can triage before SLOs get hit.

maria: good call. let's add that. example datadog monitor for kv-cache: `avg(last_15m):avg:redis.kv_hit_ratio{env:prod} < 0.85` -> slack channel #infra-alerts.

oliver: I'll add monitor docs and a sample incident automation (runbook link + playbook steps) in the monitor description so pages include it.

jake: timeline: create monitors by Thu, runbook update by Fri, staging validation next week. anyone object?

priya: works for me. I'll add steps to the runbook: detect, mitigate (scale cache / clear denom), rollback model, contact PM.

maria: final questions: who owns the long-term cost/dedup of alerts? want to create a recurring monthly review to prune noisy thresholds.

liz: I can run a monthly noise review with ops. put it on calendar: monthly, first Tue.

maria: awesome. action items recap:
- jake: create Datadog monitors + composite monitors (due Thu)
- oliver: review + QA monitors, add monitor docs
- priya: update SLO burn runbook + incident steps
- tom: validate pager routing policy in staging
- liz: schedule monthly alert noise review

jake: noted. I'll post monitor links back here when created. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Monitor creation event: datadog.create monitor_id=dd-478223 (simulated)

maria: thanks all — closing this thread after monitors are linked. we can iterate on thresholds once we have 48h of telemetry. :rocket:
